how: Members propose figures and map locations from which others can begin building.
Members repeatedly call for building, finishing and defending several figures rather than one centrally directed mark.
An ambassador answers continued difficulty with a brief promise to keep helping Sans.
The Sans proposal combines a figure and coordinates with a call for builders.
A Papyrus call receives an answer switching from individual vandalism fighting to the group effort.
Observed commitments do not test a comparative preference for bare acceptance over reasoned refusal or reveal silent placing.
Public starting and recruitment are not a necessary entry sequence when members recognize an already appearing figure and recruit its keepers.
Recognizing an explicitly uncoordinated figure can recruit its keepers without a documented public proposal or building call.
A report that the Bird appeared without subreddit or Discord coordination receives an explicit call to preserve it.
Participants judge projects too large for their people and space or too rapidly destroyed to be worthwhile.
Discouragement need not lead to moving because a complaint about rapid destruction receives encouragement to persist and subsequent progress reports.
Members dispute character identity and eye colors without demonstrating a single settled preference shared by all placers.
Builders report intermediate progress such as completed black eye pixels as a usable foundation.
Members share coordinates and reference grids and explain sending references to align individual workers.
Reference sharing and unresolved eye disagreements do not document a template settling the same design argument.
A reported script update for blue eyes receives a direct objection that scripting defeats the purpose.
Script use and prolonged repair are recorded without an explicit link establishing that defensive overload prompted script adoption.
Members invite helpers to an existing Discord, explain its coordinating advantage and promise to carry noninterference terms back there.
Individual private messages try to explain the shared work to people placing conflicting blocks.
Private explanation and an alert about a rival chat do not reveal secrecy, infiltration or the warning source.
A question about editing receives instructions on colors, placing and the waiting rule.
A question about an Ireland message receives a mutual-protection explanation and an appreciative acknowledgement.
Participants report timer constraints including an increased twenty-minute wait without establishing a site fault or successful exploit.
One room with partially unseen chat decisions cannot test the model's cross-room frequency claim or establish that organizing decisions were unnecessary.
Members protect existing figures, repair changes and put maintaining current projects before expansion.
A Temmie completion announcement receives a comment specifying the continuing maintenance it needs.
A repair caller attributes damage to rogue Irish placers while distinguishing their actions from an agreement attributed to the subreddit.
Interpret reversions alongside competing design preferences rather than infer each reverser's ignorance of an agreed change.
Keepers try to reach individual conflicting placers through private explanations, with no recorded proof that the messages settle the conflict.
A starter can welcome a changed character, so an alteration alone does not establish rejected damage or loss caused by failed communication.
One defender reports repairing instead of studying for a midterm and another recounts working until passing out.
A participant stops fighting over one figure's correction and calls it done without reporting departure from the whole canvas.
Neighbors propose peace and negotiate borders while an ambassador later reports an agreement not being honored.
Speakers identify themselves as representatives or ambassadors carrying terms between groups.
Members spare neighboring art and explicitly oppose retaliation even when their own figure is incomplete or damaged.
Peace terms include a commitment not to expand or destroy neighboring work.
Repair and border proposals are present without enough evidence to trace the proposals specifically to erosion by neighboring placers.
Visitors and members offer maintenance and reciprocal repair across neighboring works.
The later alliance explanation identifies reciprocal protection of Temmie and the Irish flag as a minimal two-room defense arrangement.
Temmie's adoption by Ireland lets the figure live within a flag under a negotiated peace arrangement.
A request for outside help against a threat does not by itself establish that the request followed an explicit shortage of defenders.
An assurance against expansion is answered with an offer to use spare turns helping the neighbor.
An Irish visitor describes stopping attacks and invites joint protection against the Void, proposing common-threat defense rather than proving universal participation.
Complaints about unhonored terms and fractured communication do not explicitly dispute binding authority or state that one agreement cannot bind every placer.
The nearest coded complaints do not state an authority limit or refusal after agreement, leaving the bounded arrow untested.
Destroyed builds prompt calls to restart figures in another position.
Members propose moving Asriel before the taskbar reaches him, distinguishing preventive relocation from rebuilding after loss.
On the successor canvas a partly built Papyrus is retained despite a nearby-location suggestion.
After a loss or failed build, participants redirect effort to another existing figure rather than relocate the same figure or leave canvas work.
An assessment that Mettaton is futile receives explicit acceptance and a return to maintaining an existing Temmie.
Members oppose trampling established art and explain its reputational cost without documenting a completed two-sided conquest debate.
Familiar Royal Guard and determination language frames defense and encouragement through the fandom's existing lore.
Members turn damaged figures into jokes such as sansdalized and a repeated unibrow.
A drinking-age joke explicitly concerns Irish Temmie's canvas damage despite its theme's blanket description as apart from the canvas.
A visitor offering help does not document being recruited into fandom membership through the canvas mark.
A helper arriving from another subreddit does not explicitly claim dual membership, divided loyalty or reassurance about belonging.
An existing fandom Discord and a spontaneously appearing figure do not document formation of a new canvas faction.
Fake merger and sequel material establish April Fools play, while an attack-call reply questions whether the call is a joke.
Canvas work is gathered in a sticky while members also object to its prominence in the host subreddit.
Members explicitly complain about the volume of canvas talk, supporting a host-attention response without proving which call caused moderation.
Host recovery includes resubmitting ordinary art and comics explicitly buried by canvas posts, not only drawing boundaries around those posts.
Host-flood complaints and an independent attack call do not show a member attacking the room's work because of those complaints.
Participants celebrate Temmie's completion and later thank defenders and allies for surviving figures.
The announcement that Temmie was made celebrates that completed achievement in the same post.
Calling a work done can end a correction struggle by accepting imperfection rather than certify conformity to a settled template.
Members retain a timelapse and recount contested facial details and surviving damage.
A participant challenges a purported final image by identifying unfinished work, meeting the revised range without assuming an organized cleanup project.
A later Papyrus build continues pixel-making on Pxls while the Irish banner retains Temmie.
Celebration and timelapse sharing occur without an explicit link establishing that celebrating produced the decision to preserve a record.
The successor build and banner continuation do not establish that a recorded artifact caused either continuation.
A member sends the Irish banner to a creator's birthday tweet while explicitly avoiding further spam.
Calls to destroy Blue and genocide Sans meet the minimal attack-call range without proving an executed raid.
Incoming hostile threats receive a survival comeback without making the visiting aggressor the room's collective voice.
A threat to destroy the dog receives a six-hours-later survival response that continues the contest in talk.
Building calls and attack proposals do not identify recruited builders turning the same hands against a rival.
An attack-call reply questions whether the call is an April Fools joke rather than giving a fully stated refusal rationale.
Separate attack proposals and peace negotiations do not document a truce invoked in answer to an attack call.
Named canvas antagonists do not establish a quarrel carried into the event from before the canvas.
The coded attack calls do not name a preexisting intergroup tie as their reason for targeting a rival.
A hostile slur and a survival reply do not show a coded objection to that slur or a dispute over hate symbols.
